reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes a multi-step SCCP process that already includes annealing and produces high strength and ductility via coherent δ and γ″ precipitates, but it does not provide evidence that a new, separate annealing step at 600–800°C will precipitate an additional ductile phase, nor does it characterize such a phase as ductile or show it enhances ductility without strength loss; the proposed mechanism and predicted outcome are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Annealing at 600–800°C can precipitate a fine, ductile secondary phase at grain boundaries and in the matrix of the specific W-based HEA.
The precipitated phase will be ductile and coherent with the matrix.
This ductile phase will enhance uniform elongation by acting as a dislocation source and barrier to crack propagation.
The coherent precipitate/matrix interface will maintain high yield strength and impact energy release.
The baseline material has a supersaturated, nanoscale coherent precipitate structure with high strength but limited ductility.
